Title: IFRS S2
Description: Sets out what an entity must disclose about its climate-related risks and opportunities, aimed at readers of general purpose financial reports. IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures.
Label: IFRS S2

Title: Sustainability Accounting Standards Board
Description: Industry-specific guidance for applying IFRS S1, used where no IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standard covers the topic. The standards name the sustainability risks and opportunities that matter most to investors in 77 industries. The independent SASB Standards Board approves them.
Label: SASB
Comment: An extension for applying IFRS information disclosure. Until now, only <10 industries relevant to project partners are selected.

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Containers and packaging entities convert metal, plastic, paper and glass into packaging products such as corrugated cardboard, aluminium cans and steel drums. Most sell business to business, and many operate globally.
Label: SASB-RT-CP

Title: SASB Industrial Machinery & Goods
Description: Industrial machinery and goods entities build equipment for construction, agriculture, energy, mining and transportation, including engines, pumps and turbines. Production consumes large amounts of steel, plastics, rubber and glass. Demand tracks industrial production, and emissions rules push efficiency improvements in the use phase.
Label: SASB-RT-IG

Title: SASB Electrical & Electronic Equipment
Description: Electrical and electronic equipment entities make power generation equipment, transformers, motors, switchboards, automation controls and cables. The scope covers building equipment such as HVAC systems and elevators, plus components like coils and wires. These entities compete globally and earn much of their revenue outside their home country.
Label: SASB-RT-EE

Title: SASB Hardware
Description: Hardware entities design and sell computers, consumer electronics, communications equipment, storage devices and peripherals. Many depend on contract manufacturers for production.
Label: SASB-TC-HW

Title: SASB Software & IT Services
Description: Software and IT services entities sell applications software, infrastructure software and middleware to retail, business and government customers. The industry also covers consulting and outsourced IT functions. Newer models include cloud computing, software as a service and machine learning. Brand value matters here because wide adoption of one product tends to drive further sales.
Label: SASB-TC-SI

Title: SASB Road Transportation
Description: Road transportation entities run long-haul and short-haul freight trucking, split between truckload and less-than-truckload carriage. Owner-operators make up most of the industry because entry is easy. A few large operators hold share through contracts with major shippers, and often subcontract to owner-operators.
Label: SASB-TR-RO

Title: Global Reporting Initiative
Description: A reporting framework that lets any organization report its impacts on the economy, the environment and people in a comparable form. Investors, policymakers and civil society also use the standards.
Label: GRI
Comment: A set of 42 files, ranging from specific materials to social aspects.

Title: Sustainability of construction works - Environmental product declarations - Core rules for the product category of construction products
Description: European standard that provides a framework for the assessment of the environmental performance of construction products. It specifies the principles and requirements for the development of Environmental Product Declarations (EPDs) for construction products, ensuring consistency and transparency in the reporting of their environmental impacts throughout their life cycle.
Label: EN 15804
Comment: We focus on the 15804+A2 Update of module D.

Title: Method to achieve circular designs of products
Description: Gives requirements and guidance for building circularity into product design and development. It helps an organization write product design rules that meet its circular business targets or legal obligations. Life cycle thinking is the core principle, and the document covers the trade-offs that arise without sacrificing safety. The focus is material efficiency.
Label: EN 45560

Title: General method for assessing the proportion of recycled material content\nin energyrelated products;
Description: Gives a general method for assessing how much recycled material an energy-related product contains. It serves as the framework for defining that assessment within specific product groups.
Label: EN 45557

Title: General methods for the assessment of the ability to repair, reuse and\nupgrade energyrelated products
Description: Gives generic criteria and methods for assessing how easily parts come out of a product for repair, reuse or upgrade.
Label: EN 45554

Title: General method for the assessment of the ability to remanufacture energy related\nproducts
Description: Gives a general method for assessing whether an energy-related product can be remanufactured, for use by technical committees writing product-specific publications. It identifies seven process steps that remanufacturing depends on.
Label: EN 45553

Title: ISO 26000
Description: Guidance on social responsibility, covering what the term means and how to turn its principles into action. It applies to any organization regardless of activity, size or location.
Label: ISO 26000
Comment: Mentions that companies should contribute to community i.e. supplies from local commerce and producers.

Title: ISO 10004
Description: Guidance on setting up processes that monitor and measure customer satisfaction. It applies to any organization and addresses customers outside the organization.
Label: ISO 10004

Title: ISO 9001:2015
Description: The quality management standard. It sets requirements for establishing, maintaining and improving a quality management system (QMS), and applies to organizations of any size or sector.
Label: ISO 9001

Title: C2C Certification Framework
Description: The Cradle to Cradle Certified Product Standard (Full Scope) assesses the circularity and sustainability of materials and products. It scores five categories: material health, product circularity, clean air and climate protection, water and soil stewardship, and social fairness.
Label: C2C
Comment: Most research paper mentions the 2016 version, but there are currently no direct link to that version. Here we roughly refer to the C2C standard from all version, until 4.1

Title: Design of Indicators for Measuring Product Performance in the Circular Economy
Description: Assesses what a circular economy indicator should measure and how to present it. The prototype uses a points-based questionnaire, which resolves to one value between a minimum and a maximum limit. A chemical processing product serves as the test case. The paper also reports that a single aggregate metric can mislead, and that the scoring rests on context-specific assumptions.
Label: CS+16
Comment: Provides a list of binary metrics with weights to consider the overall performance.

Title: Proposing an integrated indicator to measure product repairability
Description: Presents the Product Repairability Index (PRI), which scores a product from the repairability of its parts. The index combines assembly and disassembly complexity, repair instructions, spare-part availability, and self-diagnosis aids. It weights each part by how important that part is to the whole assembly. A coffee machine case study shows which parts to redesign.
Label: RM+23
Comment: 5 parameters on the product's repairability indicator are taken as inspiration for the "Design of Disassembly" indicator. Referenced info focuses on exact products e.g. with screws, tools, etc.

Title: A dataset of characterization factors for biodiversity impact assessment in OpenLCA and LCA for experts
Description: Supplies characterization factors for biodiversity impact from land occupation, calculated with the Biodiversity Value Increment (BVI) method. The factors cover the Agribalyse 3.1.1, Ecoinvent 3.10 and Sphera LCA for Experts databases at global and country level. They account for both land-use intensity and location, and ship ready to use in OpenLCA 2.1.0.
Label: JQ+25
Comment: Provides the dataset for biodiversity impact values.

Title: Valuing Biodiversity in Life Cycle Impact Assessment
Description: Proposes a life cycle impact assessment method that quantifies how land-using production affects biodiversity across broad land use classes. The default valuation rests on naturalness, and users can substitute regional conservation priorities. A consumer product serves as the worked example. The method yields output aggregated enough to compare raw materials and production routes.
Label: JPL+19
Comment: As the base definition for biodiversity value.

Title: A strategic measurement framework to monitor and evaluate circularity performance in organizations from a transition perspective
Description: Proposes a framework for measuring circularity performance at the level of a single organization. It combines general morphological analysis with two multicriteria decision-making methods, then computes composite circularity indicators and one overall Circularity Performance Index. The intended users are organizations that set their own circularity targets.
Label: FAC+21

Title: Key performance indicators for sustainable remanufacturing: A literature\nreview and methodological framework
Description: Reviews 106 Scopus papers on sustainable remanufacturing and catalogues 1021 candidate KPIs. Among the most frequently cited, 32 are economic, 16 environmental and 3 social. The social dimension is thinly covered.
Label: CM+25

Title: Indicators to Measure Efficiency in Circular Economies
Description: Defines indicators for the economic efficiency of circular economy processes and products, and models that efficiency with Data Envelopment Analysis. The indicator set follows the European Union's requirement to cover environmental impact, economic benefit and resource scarcity. It comes from a review of official reports and highly cited papers.
Label: SRS+20

Title: Ease of disassembly of products to support circular economy strategies
Description: Proposes eDiM, the ease of Disassembly Metric, which calculates disassembly time from the Maynard Operation Sequence Technique. A calculation sheet turns a sequence of actions and basic product data into a verifiable time. That makes the result usable in policy. eDiM sorts disassembly tasks into six categories, so a manufacturer can see which tasks cost the most time. An LCD monitor serves as the case study.
Label: VP+18

Title: What Do We Know About Metal Recycling Rates?
Description: Reviews recycling rates for 60 metals and defines the metrics used to report them: end-of-life recycling rate, recycled content and old scrap ratio. The picture is poor. Only 18 metals have an end-of-life recycling rate above 50%, and only niobium, lead and ruthenium exceed 50% recycled content. Weak collection and the inherent limits of recycling processes explain much of this. Cheap primary material keeps scrap prices low.
Label: GTE+11

Title: Circular economy indicators for organizations considering sustainability and business models: Plastic, textile and electro-electronic cases
Description: Develops a set of micro-level circularity indicators that tie circular economy principles to a company's business model and to the pillars of sustainability. Three Brazilian companies, each running a different circular business model, provided the test cases. Economic and social data was either missing or scattered inside those companies. That is a barrier, because many gains from circularity appear in the social dimension, such as job creation.
Label: RE+20

Title: Resource duration as a managerial indicator for Circular Economy performance
Description: Introduces the longevity indicator, which measures material retention by how long a resource stays in use. It sums the initial lifetime with the extra lifetime earned through refurbishment and through recycling. Older burden-per-value metrics cannot guide circular economy decisions, the paper argues. Precious metals in mobile phone handsets illustrate the calculation.
Label: FE+16
Comment: Provides several metrics to assess the longevity of a product.

Title: Developing a Reparability Indicator for Electronic Products
Description: Develops a reparability indicator for self-repair, meaning repair by a layperson with no specialized workshop. The scope is consumer electronics. A test of an existing indicator with 25 Dutch participants found the available guidelines poorly structured. The improved version crowdsourced criteria from an edX course and condensed roughly 2000 entries into 26 repair criteria. A group of 46 TU Delft students checked those criteria for consistency.
Label: FB+16
Comment: Survey driven, lists out several important criterias regarding repair. One of which is "Repair manual available".

Title: Design Aspects in Repairability Scoring Systems: Comparing Their Objectivity and Completeness
Description: Compares six repair scoring systems for objectivity and completeness, where objectivity means each scoring level has a quantifiable, operator-independent test. Most criteria pass both checks. The health and safety criterion does not, and the assessment of reassembly and diagnosis needs expanding. The paper also questions whether eDiM's extra accuracy justifies its harder testing compared with counting disassembly steps.
Label: DS+22

Title: A Repurposable Attribute Basis for Identifying Repurposing Opportunities in Decommissioned Products
Description: Builds a repurposable attribute basis (RAB) from 69 documented repurposing examples. A common attribute is a property both the old and the new product share, such as a material property. A transformer attribute is an action that converts one into the other, such as deforming it. The basis holds 13 common and 15 transformer attributes, and supports generating repurposing ideas.
Label: WS+24
Comment: Gives guidelines and pointers to identify repurposable components and materials in a product.

Title: An approach to measuring circularity\nPublished 2015, adapted in 2019
Description: The Material Circularity Indicator (MCI) scores how far a product's material flows move away from linear use. It also compares use duration and intensity against an industry average. The MCI combines virgin raw material mass, unrecoverable waste mass, and a utility factor for length and intensity of use.
Label: MCI+25
Comment: The base of many circularity KPI. Divided into product and company levels.

Title: Incentive alignment of brand-owner and remanufacturer towards quality certification to refurbished products
Description: Models with game theory when a brand owner and an independent remanufacturer both gain from certifying refurbished products. Certification removes the remanufacturer's quality-image disadvantage and gives the brand owner a second revenue stream. The incentives align when competition is intense and the quality-image disadvantage is large. High variance in refurbished demand narrows that window.
Label: NB+20

Title: Integrated design of remanufacturable products based on product profiles
Description: Brings remanufacturing into early product design through Remanufacturable Product Profiles (RPPs), which record what remanufactured products have in common and their typical use contexts. Statistical clustering of about 30 successfully remanufactured products produced the profiles. A tool called REPRO2 applies them to design decisions.
Label: ZP+06

Title: Product Remanufacturability Assessment Based on Design Information
Description: Assesses remanufacturability from the design data held in CAD models, so the check happens at the design stage. The metrics cover disassembly complexity, fastener accessibility, disassemblability and recoverability, combined in one framework. An automotive alternator case study validates the model.
Label: FHC+14
Comment: Defines four key technical remanufacturability metrics.

Title: The co-opetitive strategy of a closed-loop supply chain with remanufacturing
Description: Models the choice an original equipment manufacturer faces in a closed-loop supply chain. The OEM can remanufacture returned products itself and coordinate pricing with its new products. It can instead let third-party operators remanufacture and sell into the secondary market, which risks cannibalizing new product sales.
Label: CJ+12
Comment: Remanufacturing typically costs 40–60% less than manufacturing new products.

Title: Product Circularity Assessment Methodology
Description: Proposes a quantitative method for assessing circularity across the life cycle of a product made by additive manufacturing. Additive manufacturing can cut energy and material use in production, and lower material use through reuse and recycling. The paper notes that industrial applications remain scarce.
Label: ACM+17
Comment: We specifically refer to the focus on resource's circularity in terms of the reutilization of it.

Title: Dataset with updated ozone depletion characterization factors for life cycle impact assessment
Description: Supplies ozone depletion characterization factors derived from the ozone depletion potentials in the 2022 World Meteorological Organization assessment. The factors convert emissions of ozone-depleting substances into kg CFC-11-eq for life cycle assessment.
Label: AO+24
Comment: For ozone depletion reference

Title: USEtox® 2.0 Documentation
Description: Official documentation for USEtox, the UNEP and SETAC consensus model for characterizing human health and ecotoxicological impacts of chemical emissions in life cycle assessment.
Label: USEtox2.0

Title: European characterization factors for human health damage of PM10 and ozone in life cycle impact assessment
Description: Gives characterization factors for the human health effects of PM10 and ozone in Europe. Each factor expresses the change in disability adjusted life years among European inhabitants per unit change in emissions. The covered emissions are PM10, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide and non-methane volatile organic compounds.
Label: VZ+08

Title: Human health damages due to ionising radiation in life cycle impact assessment
Description: Assesses the human health damage from routine releases of radioactive material for use in life cycle assessment. Fate and exposure come from site-specific modelling of the French nuclear fuel cycle, which yields generic exposure factors. The effect analysis rests on epidemiological studies, and the paper reports damage in disability adjusted life years.
Label: FR+00

Title: COMMISSION RECOMMENDATION (EU) 2021/2279
Description: Commission Recommendation that promotes the Environmental Footprint methods for measuring and communicating the life cycle environmental performance of products and organisations.
Label: EUPEF+21
Comment: As reference for the 16 impact factors of PEF, more specifically the Annex I

Title: The WULCA consensus characterization model for water scarcity footprints: assessing impacts of water consumption based on available water remaining (AWARE)
Description: Presents a water scarcity midpoint method agreed over a two-year consensus process by the WULCA working group of the UNEP-SETAC Life Cycle Initiative. The method supports water scarcity footprint assessment in LCA.
Label: BA+17

Title: Abiotic resource depletion in LCA
Description: Abiotic depletion potential measures the use of non-renewable resources for energy production, and an LCA assesses it as one of its factors. This study limits the definition to non-renewable resources and excludes renewable abiotic resources such as wind and flowing water.
Label: OL+02
Comment: A part of the LCA handbook, specifically for calculating the Abiotic Depletion Potential (ADP)

Title: Acidification terrestrial and freshwater
Description: Accumulated Exceedance (AE) characterizes the change in critical load exceedance for sensitive terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems where acidifying substances deposit.
Label: ILCD2011

Title: ReCiPE 2008: A life cycle impact assessment method which comprises harmonised category indicators at the midpoint and the endpoint level
Description: Describes a life cycle impact assessment method that uses one set of modelling choices but reports at both midpoint and endpoint level. The first phase compared the two main approaches to impact assessment. It focused on how impact categories and category indicators get chosen, and how characterization models convert inventory results into indicator results.
Label: ReCiPe2008

Title: LCIA Method Data set: Eutrophication potential - freshwater
Description: Exposure factors for water-borne emissions come from the CARMEN model, and those for air-borne emissions from EUTREND. The model covers impacts on freshwater systems only.
Label: EUEP-FW

Title: Assessing water circularity in cities: Methodological framework with a\ncase study
Description: Gives a quantitative tool for measuring water circularity inside engineered urban water infrastructure, and applies it to macro-level water planning and policy.
Label: AM+22
Comment: The diagram gives an overview of the metrics we included here.

Title: ESRS E1 Climate change
Description: European Sustainability Reporting Standard on climate change (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772). Includes Disclosure Requirement E1-6 — Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and Total GHG emissions.
Label: ESRS E1

Title: ISO 14067:2018 Greenhouse gases — Carbon footprint of products
Description: Specifies principles, requirements and guidelines for quantifying the carbon footprint of a product (CFP), based on life cycle assessment.
Label: ISO 14067

Title: ISO 14044
Description: Environmental management — Life cycle assessment — Requirements and guidelines
Label: ISO 14044

Title: ISO 14046
Description: Environmental management — Water footprint — Principles, requirements and guidelines
Label: ISO 14046

Title: ISO 59020
Description: Circular economy — Measuring and assessing circularity performance
Label: ISO 59020

Title: PSILCA
Description: Product Social Impact Life Cycle Assessment database
Label: PSILCA

Title: ESRS S1
Description: European Sustainability Reporting Standard S1 — Own workforce
Label: ESRS S1

Title: Cradle to Cradle Certified Product Standard
Description: “Preparing for Active Cycling” — designing and enabling the product to be recovered and cycled (recycled or composted) at end of use. Section 5.2, Product Circularity category, Cradle to Cradle Certified Product Standard v4.1.
Label: C2C 5.2

Title: Cradle to Cradle Certified Product Standard
Description: “Increasing Demand: Incorporating Cycled and/or Renewable Content” — the share of cycled (recycled) and/or renewable content in the product. Section 5.3, Product Circularity category, Cradle to Cradle Certified Product Standard v4.1.
Label: C2C 5.3

Title: ESRS E1 Climate change
Description: Targets related to climate change mitigation and adaptation. Disclosure Requirement E1-4 of ESRS E1 Climate change (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E1-4

Title: ESRS E1 Climate change
Description: Energy consumption and mix. Disclosure Requirement E1-5 of ESRS E1 Climate change (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E1-5

Title: ESRS E1 Climate change
Description: Gross Scopes 1, 2, 3 and total GHG emissions. Disclosure Requirement E1-6 of ESRS E1 Climate change (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E1-6

Title: ESRS E3 Water and marine resources
Description: European Sustainability Reporting Standard on water and marine resources, including water consumption, withdrawals and discharges (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E3-4

Title: ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy
Description: Actions and resources related to resource use and the circular economy. Disclosure Requirement E5-2 of ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E5-2

Title: ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy
Description: Resource inflows — the materials used by the undertaking and their circularity. Disclosure Requirement E5-4 of ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E5-4

Title: ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy
Description: Resource outflows — the products, materials and waste leaving the undertaking. Disclosure Requirement E5-5 of ESRS E5 Resource use and circular economy (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS E5-5

Title: ESRS S1 Own workforce
Description: Policies related to the undertaking's own workforce. Disclosure Requirement S1-1 of ESRS S1 Own workforce (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS S1-1

Title: ESRS S1 Own workforce
Description: Health and safety metrics for the undertaking's own workforce. Disclosure Requirement S1-14 of ESRS S1 Own workforce (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS S1-14

Title: ESRS S1 Own workforce
Description: Characteristics of the undertaking's employees. Disclosure Requirement S1-6 of ESRS S1 Own workforce (Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772).
Label: ESRS S1-6

Title: GRI 101: Biodiversity 2024
Description: GRI 101 sets out reporting requirements on biodiversity, including impacts on ecosystems, species and habitats across operations and the supply chain.
Label: GRI 101

Title: GRI 2: General Disclosures 2021
Description: GRI 2 contains disclosures about an organization's reporting practices, activities, workers, governance, strategy and policies.
Label: GRI 2-7

Title: GRI 201: Economic Performance 2016
Description: GRI 201 covers economic performance, including the direct economic value generated and distributed by an organization.
Label: GRI 201-1

Title: GRI 301: Materials 2016
Description: GRI 301 covers materials used by weight or volume, recycled input materials, and reclaimed products and their packaging.
Label: GRI 301-3

Title: GRI 302: Energy 2016
Description: Energy consumption outside of the organization — upstream and downstream energy use across the value chain. Disclosure 302-2 of GRI 302: Energy 2016.
Label: GRI 302-2

Title: GRI 302: Energy 2016
Description: Energy intensity — energy consumption relative to an organization-specific denominator (e.g. per unit of output). Disclosure 302-3 of GRI 302: Energy 2016.
Label: GRI 302-3

Title: GRI 302: Energy 2016
Description: Reduction of energy consumption achieved as a direct result of conservation and efficiency initiatives. Disclosure 302-4 of GRI 302: Energy 2016.
Label: GRI 302-4

Title: GRI 302: Energy 2016
Description: Reductions in the energy requirements of products and services. Disclosure 302-5 of GRI 302: Energy 2016.
Label: GRI 302-5

Title: GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018
Description: Topic standard on water withdrawal, discharge and consumption, and the management of water-related impacts. GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018.
Label: GRI 303

Title: GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018
Description: Management of water discharge-related impacts, including the minimum standards set for effluent quality. Disclosure 303-2 of GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018.
Label: GRI 303-2

Title: GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018
Description: Water discharge — total volume of water discharged by destination, with quality and treatment. Disclosure 303-4 of GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018.
Label: GRI 303-4

Title: GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018
Description: Water consumption — total water consumed, including consumption in water-stressed areas. Disclosure 303-5 of GRI 303: Water and Effluents 2018.
Label: GRI 303-5

Title: GRI 306: Waste 2020
Description: Waste generated — total weight of waste generated, broken down by composition. Disclosure 306-3 of GRI 306: Waste 2020.
Label: GRI 306-3

Title: GRI 306: Waste 2020
Description: Waste diverted from disposal — waste recovered through preparation for reuse, recycling and other recovery operations. Disclosure 306-4 of GRI 306: Waste 2020.
Label: GRI 306-4

Title: GRI 308: Supplier Environmental Assessment 2016
Description: GRI 308 covers the screening and assessment of suppliers using environmental criteria.
Label: GRI 308-1

Title: GRI 401: Employment 2016
Description: GRI 401 covers employment, including new employee hires, employee turnover, and benefits provided to employees.
Label: GRI 401-1

Title: GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018
Description: Topic standard on occupational health and safety: management systems, hazard identification and risk management, worker participation, and work-related injuries and ill health. GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018.
Label: GRI 403

Title: GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018
Description: Work-related ill health — fatalities and recordable cases of work-related ill health, and the main types. Disclosure 403-10 of GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018.
Label: GRI 403-10

Title: GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018
Description: Work-related injuries — rates and numbers of fatalities, high-consequence injuries and recordable work-related injuries. Disclosure 403-9 of GRI 403: Occupational Health and Safety 2018.
Label: GRI 403-9

Title: GRI 416: Customer Health and Safety 2016
Description: Topic standard on the health and safety impacts of products and services on customers. GRI 416: Customer Health and Safety 2016.
Label: GRI 416

Title: GRI 416: Customer Health and Safety 2016
Description: Incidents of non-compliance concerning the health and safety impacts of products and services. Disclosure 416-2 of GRI 416: Customer Health and Safety 2016.
Label: GRI 416-2

Title: ISO 14021
Description: Environmental labels and declarations — Self-declared environmental claims (Type II environmental labelling).
Label: ISO 14021

Title: Time-based disassembly method: how to assess the best disassembly sequence and time of target components in complex products
Description: Proposes a time-based method to determine the optimal disassembly sequence and to estimate the disassembly time of target components in complex products.
Label: MM+17

Title: EN 15804+A2 Module D
Description: Core rules for construction-product Environmental Product Declarations; Module D reports benefits and loads beyond the system boundary (reuse, recovery and recycling potential).
Label: Module D - EN15804+A2

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Number of recalls issued and total units recalled. SASB RT-CP-250a.1 (Containers & Packaging — Product Safety).
Label: SASB RT-250a.1

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Air emissions of NOx (excluding N₂O), SOx, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and particulate matter (PM). SASB RT-CP-120a.1 (Containers & Packaging — Air Quality).
Label: SASB RT-CP-120a.1

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Total energy consumed, percentage grid electricity, percentage renewable, and total self-generated energy. SASB RT-CP-130a.1 (Containers & Packaging — Energy Management).
Label: SASB RT-CP-130a.1

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Total water withdrawn and total water consumed, with the percentage of each in regions with High or Extremely High Baseline Water Stress. SASB RT-CP-140a.1 (Containers & Packaging — Water Management).
Label: SASB RT-CP-140a.1

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Revenue from products that are reusable, recyclable, or compostable. SASB RT-CP-410a.2 (Containers & Packaging — Product Lifecycle Management).
Label: SASB RT-CP-410a.2

Title: SASB Electrical & Electronic Equipment
Description: Total energy consumed, percentage grid electricity, and percentage renewable. SASB RT-EE-130a.1 (Electrical & Electronic Equipment — Energy Management).
Label: SASB RT-EE-130a.1

Title: SASB Industrial Machinery & Goods
Description: Revenue from remanufactured products and remanufacturing services, including discussion of efforts to obtain end-of-life products and parts for remanufacture. SASB RT-IG-440b.1 (Industrial Machinery & Goods — Remanufacturing Design & Services).
Label: SASB RT-IG-440b.1

Title: SASB Containers & Packaging
Description: Gross global Scope 1 emissions and the percentage covered under emissions-limiting regulations. SASB RT-CP-110a.1 (Containers & Packaging — Greenhouse Gas Emissions).
Label: SASB-RT-CP-110a.1

Title: Environmental impact and water footprint of biofuel production from macro-algae biomass based on life cycle assessment
Description: Life cycle assessment quantifying the environmental impact and water footprint of biofuel produced from macro-algae biomass.
Label: TF+25

Title: Remanufacturing (Reman) – Quality classification for circular processes
Description: DIN SPEC 91472:2023-06. Specifies value-retention processes and a quality classification for remanufacturing (Reman) within circular processes — process chain, classification, and the process-quality matrix.
Label: DIN SPEC 91472

Title: GRI 414: Supplier Social Assessment 2016
Description: GRI 414 covers the screening and assessment of suppliers using social criteria. Disclosure 414-1 — New suppliers that were screened using social criteria — reports the percentage of new suppliers screened using social criteria (human rights, labour, health & safety and related topics).
Label: GRI 414-1

Title: GRI 204: Procurement Practices 2016
Description: GRI 204 addresses an organization's procurement practices, including support for local suppliers. Disclosure 204-1 — Proportion of spending on local suppliers — reports the percentage of the procurement budget spent on suppliers local to significant locations of operation, with the organization's definition of 'local'.
Label: GRI 204-1
